source: Hernandez, Schmidt, Okudan (2013) Systematic ideation effectiveness study of TRIZ
finding: Controlled student ideation study, TRIZ vs ad hoc control. TRIZ raised novelty and variety and slightly lowered quantity.
numbers: Two sites (UTEP, UMD), analysed with PSU. Task: redesign an LED traffic light that gathers snow. Metrics: quantity, novelty, variety. Group sizes not seen in the abstract.
quote: TRIZ does improve the ideation effectiveness metrics Novelty and Variety while slightly reducing Quantity
limits: Abstract only was read (Crossref text). Exact effect sizes and N not seen. Single task. Students, not experts.
agent_relevance: Best classical evidence that a TRIZ-guided step buys novelty and costs volume. Fits a typed reframe used only when diversity is needed, not for speed.

source: Cok et al. (2026) Evaluating TRIZ with and without LLM support: an experimental study on engineering problem solving (DESIGN 2026)
finding: Students used the TRIZ contradiction matrix with and without an LLM on three problems. The LLM did not always improve design quality on complex tasks, but it lowered workload, improved understanding of contradictions and raised perceived usefulness.
numbers: Three problems. N and effect sizes not given in the abstract page.
limits: Abstract page only. Subjective measures dominate. Outcome depended strongly on prompting experience.
agent_relevance: Human-side result: LLM help with the matrix improves comfort more than quality. Do not assume a typed reframe raises answer quality; test it.

source: Jiang and Luo (2024) AutoTRIZ: Artificial ideation with TRIZ and LLMs (DETC2024 / arXiv 2403.13002)
finding: AutoTRIZ makes the LLM name one improving and one worsening parameter, then looks up principles in a fixed 39x39 matrix (code, not model), then writes solutions. Contradiction detection was unstable across repeated runs.
numbers: 10 textbook cases. Each run 100 times. Entropy scale 0 to 6.64. 7 of 10 cases fully or half matched the textbook pair within the top 3 detections. Only 4 cases (5,6,7,8) had a dominant top answer; 2 were complete matches. In almost all cases one parameter stayed fixed and the other varied.
limits: Tiny case base. Textbook answers are not a gold standard (authors say so). No novelty or quality comparison against a baseline in this version. Case 7 chosen because it was consistent.
agent_relevance: Matches our split: code does the lookup, model fills the slot. But the slot (parameter choice) is noisy, so vote over many runs and keep only the stable parameter.

source: Jiang and Luo (2024) AutoTRIZ, same paper: self-consistency finding
finding: Outputs with higher frequency across 100 runs matched the textbook better. Frequency is a usable confidence signal for the reframe choice.
numbers: Across all 10 cases, higher-probability detections within the top 3 aligned better with the textbook reference. Authors suggest self-consistency may help.
limits: Pattern described qualitatively, no test statistic. Same-model samples are not independent (our G4).
agent_relevance: Use repeat-sample agreement only as a hint to pick which contradiction to try first, never as proof the reframe is right.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT: An LLM-augmented method for problem-solving (arXiv 2408.05897)
finding: Chain-of-thought gave the best recall of expert contradiction pairs with GPT-4 but precision stayed low. Few-shot lowered recall.
numbers: 37 classic cases (collection A), 34 tested after 3 used as shots. Recall/precision: basic 0.675/0.259, CoT 0.691/0.310, few-shot 0.245/0.333, CoT+few-shot 0.247/0.298. Basic prompt: 85.3% of cases and CoT: 88.2% hit at least half the parameters of the literature pair.
limits: Ground truth is one published pair per case; many valid pairs exist, so precision is understated. Cases may be in training data. GPT-4 only for this step.
agent_relevance: Few-shot examples can shrink the number of reframes the model proposes. Ask for several contradictions, then filter in code.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT: solution step
finding: Solution quality (embedding similarity to the published solution) did not differ between four prompt strategies.
numbers: 84 cases, text-embedding-ada-002 cosine similarity, temperature 1. Means: base 0.829 (SD 0.031), CoT 0.823 (0.031), few-shot 0.824 (0.030), CoT+few-shot 0.824 (0.033). No significant difference.
limits: Cosine similarity to a known solution rewards recall of known answers, not novelty. The principle was supplied from the literature, so this tests writing, not choosing.
agent_relevance: A given principle already steers the model; fancy prompting adds nothing here. The hard part is choosing the principle, not applying it.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT: GPT-3.5 versus GPT-4 on new cases
finding: GPT-4 beat GPT-3.5 at recovering contradiction pairs on cases published after the training cutoff. The gap grows with task complexity.
numbers: 10 cases after April 2023, average 5.5 contradiction pairs per case. CoT recall: GPT-4 0.544, GPT-3.5 0.400. Basic prompt recall 0.544 vs 0.400. GPT-3.5 omitted parameter numbers in 2 of 10 cases; GPT-4 never did.
limits: 10 cases only. Post-cutoff control is good practice but sample is small.
agent_relevance: Contamination control: test reframes on problems newer than the model. Weaker models fail on format, so add code-side schema checks.

source: Trapp and Warschat (2024) LLM-based extraction of contradictions from patents (arXiv 2403.14258)
finding: Zero-shot GPT-4 found contradiction sentences in patents about as well as fine-tuned classifiers, but it also found contradictions in patents humans marked as having none.
numbers: 100 patents with annotated contradictions: recall 0.71, precision 0.46, F1 0.56; mean 3.81 annotated sentences, 2.69 found, 3.19 false positives. Best PaTRIZ fine-tuned: weighted F1 0.54. BERTScore F1 0.93 (sentences), 0.88 (summary). On 100 patents annotated as contradiction-free, GPT-4 found contradictions in 86.
limits: Annotations may be wrong (authors show a golf-ball patent where GPT-4 looks right). Cannot separate model over-detection from label error. Only gpt-4-1106-preview.
agent_relevance: An LLM will see a trade-off in almost any text. A reframe operator that fires whenever the model says it found a contradiction will fire too often; gate it on a failing check (G1).

source: Trapp and Warschat (2024), parameter mapping part
finding: Mapping concrete parameters to the 39 abstract TRIZ parameters was judged by the authors on examples, not scored against labels.
numbers: Case studies on patents US06938300 and US07543344 and the golf ball patent; no accuracy number for the 39-parameter mapping.
limits: Qualitative only. Prior PaTRIZ pipelines reached only F1 0.37 and 0.65 on its two classifier parts.
agent_relevance: The 39-parameter abstraction step has no measured accuracy in this paper. Treat it as unvalidated.

source: TRIZBench (2026) dataset and benchmark for TRIZ reasoning (Findings of ACL 2026)
finding: Largest TRIZ-LLM benchmark so far. Finding: detecting that a contradiction exists is easy, naming the right improving/worsening pair is hard, and principle choice works best when the TRIZ matrix structure is used.
numbers: 1,354 TRIZ cases from 590 sources, 1,679 contradictions, 2,630 solutions, 429 US patents (257 with parameter labels, 304 with principle labels). Expert audit of 200 cases: pre-adjudication agreement 74.0%.
limits: Labels come from open technical sources, so coverage bias. Only 29.2% of contradictions have TRIZ parameters. US patents only. Classical 39/40 sets only.
agent_relevance: Strongest current evidence. Anchors the claim that the weak step is the abstraction to a typed contradiction, not the final idea.

source: TRIZBench: contradiction prediction (Table 2)
finding: Models detect that a contradiction exists far better than they match the exact improve/worsen pair. Few-shot gave small and inconsistent changes. LoRA helped.
numbers: Case-level HasF1 vs PairF1: Qwen3-8B FS 0.84 vs 0.31; Qwen3-32B ZS 0.87 vs 0.30; Gemini-2.5-Pro ZS 0.76 vs 0.36, FS 0.77 vs 0.42. Patent Hit@3 for pair: 0.13 to 0.26 for prompted LLMs; PatentSBERTa retrieval 0.23 (case PairF1 0.45); best LoRA: detection F1 0.90, patent Hit@3 0.28.
limits: Semantic matching threshold 0.65. Table column alignment in the PDF text was parsed by hand. Patent pair choice is only top-3 hit.
agent_relevance: Typed reframes will often pick the wrong pair (about 3 in 4 misses at best). Keep several candidate pairs alive and let a real check pick.

source: TRIZBench: inventive principle prediction (Table 3)
finding: Looking up the contradiction matrix beat free LLM prompting at picking principles. Best was an LLM reranking the matrix candidates.
numbers: Matrix lookup Hit@3: 0.67 on cases, 0.48 on patents. Matrix-Rerank (Qwen3-8B): Hit@3 0.71 case, 0.59 patent (Recall@3 0.29 and 0.47). TF-IDF text retrieval: 0.69 / 0.56 Hit@3. LLM zero-shot Qwen3-8B 0.39 case, 0.27 patent; Gemini-2.5-Pro ZS 0.45 / 0.31, FS 0.52 / 0.35. End-to-end Qwen3-8B ZS-Rerank 0.59 / 0.46.
limits: Hit@3 over 40 principles has a high chance baseline (3 of 40 is 7.5% for one gold principle, more with several gold). No random baseline reported in the pages read. Gold principles are those cited in a source, not proven best.
agent_relevance: Direct support for our design: code does the matrix lookup, the model only reranks or applies. Free-form 'which of the 40 principles?' prompting is the weakest option.

source: TRIZBench: grounded reasoning (Figure 3)
finding: Principle accuracy rose with how well the model cited patent sentences describing the mechanism. Label accuracy alone can mislead.
numbers: Evidence F1 rises with more evidence sentences; PatentSBERTa retrieval best, +0.14 F1 over TF-IDF. Example: right parameter pair and Hit@3=1 with missing evidence for the improving side; another case had evidence F1=1.0 with a wrong pair.
limits: Correlation shown in a figure, no coefficient in the text read. Retrieved evidence sets are used as references, not human gold.
agent_relevance: Make reframes cite the source text that supports each parameter. A reframe with no supporting span should not count as a pass.

source: TRIZBench: small human calibration
finding: Humans showed the same pattern as models: easier to see that there is a contradiction than to map it to the right pair, even for people who know TRIZ.
numbers: 5 cases, 6 participants across three background levels, plus several frontier models.
limits: Very small. Details are in an appendix not read.
agent_relevance: The hard step is hard for people too, so the matrix is not a shortcut around judgement.

source: Xu, Wu, Zhao (2026) TRIZ-RAGNER (arXiv 2602.23656)
finding: Retrieval of TRIZ knowledge plus reranking lifted exact matching of the improving/worsening parameters in patent sentences above plain GPT and above classic NER.
numbers: PaTRIZ dataset, 8:1:1 split, 3 seeds. Classic baselines F1 60.7 to 71.7%. GPT zero-shot 73.7%, prompt-engineered GPT 76.9%. TRIZ-RAGNER precision 85.6, recall 82.9, F1 84.2 (+7.3 points over best baseline). Ablations: without retrieval 78.1; without reranking 79.8; another LLM-component ablation 76.6.
limits: Sentence-level NER on one expert dataset, not problem solving. Hyperparameters tuned on the validation split. Single paper, no independent replication.
agent_relevance: Grounding the model in TRIZ definitions helps the abstraction step. Supports giving the agent a short typed glossary at reframe time.

source: Szczepanik and Chudziak (2025) TRIZ Agents: multi-agent LLM approach (arXiv 2506.18783)
finding: Multi-agent TRIZ pipeline with specialist roles was shown on one gantry-crane case only. No measured comparison to a plain model.
numbers: One case study (gantry crane swing). Six workflow steps. No quantitative score. Authors note a missing feedback loop and context window limits.
limits: Anecdote. No baseline, no human rating.
agent_relevance: Not evidence that role agents help. Matches our G4 warning on persona voters.

source: Liu, Huang, Wang (2026) TRIZ-a: agent evolution with TRIZ operators (arXiv 2610.04555)
finding: Closest published match to O4 and O8: principles turned into typed code-transformation operators, each candidate declaring a contradiction and operator before its result is known, with hard promotion gates. Gains were small to moderate and not attributed to TRIZ.
numbers: Three cybersecurity datasets, paired reruns. F1 gains +2.88, +4.23, +0.15 points. 45-activity CICIoT2023 campaign: macro-F1 0.8325 to 0.8483 (+0.0158, 1.90% relative), 43 of 45 family-seed groups improved, but it failed the frozen gate (needs +3.2277% relative and FPR drop of 0.005).
quote: the comparisons do not determine whether the improvements came from TRIZ guidance, FI/Ideality, or another part of the workflow
limits: No matched-budget ablation, so gains cannot be credited to TRIZ rather than to search itself. Authors say this directly. One domain. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Declare-before-result and gate-before-promote is the pattern we want. But it is untested whether TRIZ typing beats untyped mutation at equal compute (our G7).

source: Lee et al. (2026) TRIZ-inspired text-to-CAD (arXiv 2606.21378)
finding: Telling the LLM the contradiction and a named principle gave more controlled trade-offs than a vanilla 'make it lighter' prompt, which over-cut mass and raised stress sharply.
numbers: One chair, FEA at 900 N, strength(#14) vs weight(#1). Mass change: vanilla -31.8% with stress +64.1% and deflection +99.4%; Segmentation -14.7%, stress -0.1%; Anti-weight -5.9%, stress +21.6%; Dynamics -4.0%, stress +33.2%; Composite -10.0%, stress +40.7%, deflection +44.4%.
limits: One object, one run each, no repeats, no creativity rating. Baseline chair had huge safety margin (1.7% of yield). The vanilla prompt was not told to hold stress.
agent_relevance: Typed principles gave a spread of distinct trade-off points, one of them nearly free. A checkable physical measure made the comparison honest.

source: Bose (2026) IdeaForge (arXiv 2605.13311)
finding: Claims that mixing TRIZ with Design Thinking and SCAMPER agents gives more diverse candidates than single-method baselines, using a heuristic score.
numbers: One legal-technology use case. TRIZ claim scored highest on the authors' InnovationScore (0.500) because it collected the most CONVERGENT links. Weights are heuristic.
limits: Score built by the authors, no human experts, no external baseline numbers. Convergence between methods all driven by one LLM, so not independent.
agent_relevance: Cross-method agreement from one model is not independent evidence (G4). Do not copy.

source: Ilevbare, Probert, Phaal (2013) A review of TRIZ, and its benefits and challenges in practice (Technovation)
finding: Major review of TRIZ in practice. Only the title and venue were seen this session, not the text.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened. Do not cite findings from it until read.
agent_relevance: Should be read for the list of reported benefits and reported barriers.

source: Dumas and Schmidt (2015) Relational reasoning as predictor for engineering ideation success using TRIZ (J Engineering Design)
finding: Title indicates that relational reasoning ability predicts success with TRIZ ideation, a moderator by individual difference. Text not seen.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened; publisher page returned 403.
agent_relevance: If true, TRIZ gain depends on the user's analogy skill, which would also apply to a model's abstraction step. Verify first.

source: Livotov, Chandra Sekaran, Masudah (2019) Lower abstraction level of TRIZ inventive principles improves ideation productivity of engineering students
finding: Title indicates that more concrete versions of the 40 principles raised student ideation productivity. Text not seen.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened; publisher redirected to login.
agent_relevance: Would suggest giving the model concrete worked examples of each principle rather than the 40 bare names. Verify first.

source: Chang, Chien, Yu, Chu (2016) Effect of TRIZ on the creativity of engineering students (Thinking Skills and Creativity)
finding: Title only. A TRIZ course effect study on engineering student creativity. Text not seen.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Candidate for effect sizes on trained students. Verify first.

source: Hernandez et al. earlier versions (2006 and 2012 DETC) of the TRIZ ideation study
finding: Crossref lists an earlier 2006 conference paper on TRIZ ideation effectiveness and a 2012 conference version of the 2013 study. Not read.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened. No independent lab replication of the 2013 study was found in the lists I saw; absence is not proof.
agent_relevance: Treat the 2013 novelty gain as single-lab evidence until a replication is found.

source: Coverage note: 2020-2026 LLM+TRIZ literature on arXiv
finding: arXiv listing for TRIZ shows 33 results; the LLM-related ones are AutoTRIZ, TRIZ-GPT, patent contradiction extraction (all 2024), TRIZ Agents (2025), TRIZ-RAGNER, IdeaForge, text-to-CAD (2026) and TRIZ-a (Oct 2026). None of these is a head-to-head test of TRIZ prompts against a plain prompt on ideation quality with blind judges.
numbers: 7 LLM+TRIZ arXiv papers read. 0 compare a TRIZ-structured prompt with a matched-token plain prompt on blind-rated novelty or correctness.
limits: Search APIs (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, arXiv API) were rate-limited and the second web search was refused, so journal-only papers (AutoTRIZ journal version, Adv. Eng. Informatics 2025) were not read in full.
agent_relevance: The central open question for O4 and O8 (does a typed reframe beat plain sampling at equal tokens) is untested in the literature I found. We must measure it ourselves.

source: Mohammadi and Zeng (2025) Enhancing TRIZ through environment-based design supported by an LLM (AI EDAM)
finding: Abstract says an LLM-led question-asking step before TRIZ helps find functions and conflicts, and that the approach generated ideas to resolve contradictions. Notes TRIZ is criticised for weak problem formulation.
numbers: No numbers in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only (Crossref). Evaluation reported qualitatively.
agent_relevance: Supports spending effort on problem formulation before applying principles, in line with O4 reframing.
